emergencyNumber: 117 (police), 118 (fire). No unified emergency number; go directly to a hospital for medical emergencies.
healthcareSystem: Public healthcare system with very limited infrastructure. Hospitals in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire provide basic care. Private clinics offer better services but at higher cost. Rural healthcare is extremely limited.
qualityNotes: Healthcare quality is low by international standards. Brazzaville has the best facilities, including the CHU (Centre Hospitalier Universitaire) de Brazzaville. Private clinics in major cities offer better care. Equipment shortages, drug stock-outs, and limited specialist availability are common. Serious conditions require evacuation.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 8am-6pm weekdays, shorter on Saturday. Very limited availability outside Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire.
pharmacyTips: Bring all medications you will need from home. Counterfeit drugs are a concern — buy only from established pharmacies. Stock may be limited even in Brazzaville. Staff speak French.
prescriptionRules: Prescription medications require a doctor's ordonnance. In practice, many medications are sold without strict enforcement. Bring all needed medications from home as availability is unreliable.

restrictedMeds.name: Controlled narcotics
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter and prescription documentation for any controlled substances.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Requires documentation. Keep medications in original packaging with prescription.

bringDocumentation: Bring all prescriptions, a doctor's letter listing medications, copies of your travel insurance, and vaccination certificates (especially yellow fever). French translations are helpful.

travelInsurance.tips: Essential for travel to the Congo. Ensure your policy covers medical evacuation to South Africa or Europe, as local facilities cannot handle serious conditions. Many facilities require cash payment upfront.

recommended: Routine vaccinations (MMR, diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis, varicella, polio, flu)
vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever vaccination is REQUIRED for entry. Malaria is widespread — take prophylaxis and use mosquito nets and repellent. Consult a travel medicine clinic 4-6 weeks before departure.

waterNotes: Tap water is NOT safe to drink anywhere in the country. Use only bottled or purified water for drinking and brushing teeth. Avoid ice unless confirmed made from purified water.
foodSafetyTips: Eat only thoroughly cooked food served hot. Avoid raw vegetables, salads, and unpeeled fruits. Street food carries higher risk. Stick to bottled beverages. Wash hands frequently.
medicalTourismNote: Republic of the Congo is not a medical tourism destination. Patients with serious conditions are typically evacuated to South Africa, Morocco, or France.
sources: U.S. Embassy in the Republic of the Congo
French Ministry of Foreign Affairs Travel Advisory

hospitals.name: CHU de Brazzaville (Centre Hospitalier Universitaire)
hospitals.notes: Main public hospital. French-speaking. Basic equipment and frequent supply shortages. Emergency department available.

hospitals.name: Clinique Médico-Chirurgicale de Brazzaville
hospitals.notes: Private clinic offering better care than public facilities. French-speaking. Cash payment typically required upfront.

hospitals.name: Republic of the Congo General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Government facility. Limited English. Bring a translator app.

dentalCare.availability: Very limited. A few dental clinics in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire. None in rural areas.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care quality is basic. Sterilization standards may not meet international norms. Bring any needed dental supplies.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, seek a private clinic in Brazzaville. Consider evacuation for complex dental procedures.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Extremely limited. No established English-speaking mental health services.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are very limited. Consider telehealth with your home-country provider. The stigma around mental health remains significant.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is extremely limited throughout the country.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Hospitals have minimal accessibility features. Wheelchair access is not standard.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Roads are often unpaved and difficult to navigate.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Travelers with mobility challenges should plan carefully and consider hiring local assistance. Contact your hotel in advance about accessibility.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mandatory mask requirements. May be requested in healthcare facilities.
covidStatus.testing: Limited COVID testing available at major hospitals in Brazzaville.
covidStatus.notes: Healthcare capacity for respiratory illness is limited. Bring personal protective equipment if concerned.

insuranceClaimProcess: Most facilities require cash payment upfront. Obtain detailed receipts and medical reports. Insurance claims are typically submitted after returning home. Keep all documentation including itemized bills.

commonCosts.currency: XAF (Central African CFA Franc), prices shown in USD equivalent
commonCosts.note: Private clinic costs are significantly higher than public facilities. Cash payment is standard. Costs are low compared to Western countries but high relative to local incomes.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation is essential for serious conditions. Ensure travel insurance specifically covers evacuation from Central Africa. International SOS has a presence in the region.
